transcript.heading: News Report One (British Female)
paras: An independent bookstore in Edinburgh has launched an innovative "blind date with a book" campaign to encourage customers to discover new authors and genres. Instead of displaying books with their covers showing, staff wrap books in plain paper, writing only a few intriguing clues about the story on the outside - things like "set in Paris in the 1920s," "features a mystery-solving cat," or "guaranteed to make you cry happy tears." Customers choose books based on these clues without knowing the title or author until they purchase and unwrap them. Since the campaign began two months ago, book sales have increased by forty percent, and many customers have returned to report finding new favorite authors they never would have chosen otherwise. The bookstore has also started a monthly book club where readers discuss their blind date books. Other bookstores across the UK have begun adopting the idea, creating a new way to connect readers with books they might otherwise overlook.
Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

2. How much have sales increased since the campaign began?

transcript.heading: News Report Two (American Male)
paras: A new study published in the Journal of Gerontology finds that regular gardening can provide significant physical and mental health benefits for older adults. Researchers followed over three thousand adults aged sixty and older for eight years, tracking their activity levels, health outcomes, and life satisfaction. Those who gardened at least two or three times per week had lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, and obesity compared to non-gardeners, and also reported better balance and hand strength, reducing their risk of falls. The physical activity involved in digging, planting, weeding, and harvesting provides moderate exercise that is easy on aging joints. Gardeners also scored significantly higher on measures of life satisfaction and lower on depression scales, likely due to a combination of outdoor activity, connection to nature, and the sense of accomplishment from growing food or flowers. The study recommends that community programs increase access to gardening spaces for senior citizens.
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

transcript.heading: News Report Three (American Female)
paras: Public schools in Portland, Oregon, are making major changes to their lunch programs, with a goal of sourcing over fifty percent of food from local farms and producers by next year. The initiative is part of a broader effort to serve healthier, fresher meals while supporting local agriculture and reducing the environmental impact of transporting food long distances. Already, thirty percent of produce served in school cafeterias comes from farms within a hundred-mile radius, including apples, pears, leafy greens, and root vegetables that are in season. Students have responded positively to the changes, with school officials reporting a twenty percent increase in students eating school lunch rather than bringing food from home. Meal planners are also working to create menus that reflect the cultural diversity of the student body, incorporating dishes inspired by Mexican, Vietnamese, and Somali cuisine using fresh local ingredients. The program has become a model for other school districts across the country.

transcript.heading: Conversation One (American Female + American Male)
paras: Woman (Chloe): Hey Josh, I need your help. I'm planning a surprise birthday party for my girlfriend Emma next Saturday, and I have no idea what I'm doing.
Man (Josh): Oh, that's so sweet, Chloe! I'd love to help. What have you planned so far?
Woman: Absolutely nothing. That's why I need you. I know you love planning parties. I don't even know where to start.
Man: Okay, first things first - how many people do you want to invite? And do you want to have it at your apartment, or somewhere else?
Woman: I was thinking maybe twenty people - close friends and her family. But my apartment is pretty small. I don't think I can fit twenty people there.

Man: You could rent the back room at that Italian restaurant downtown, or maybe have it at the park if the weather's nice. But since it's a surprise, maybe having it at a restaurant is easier - you don't have to clean or cook.
Woman: That's a good point. But restaurants can be expensive. What if I ask our friend Tyler if we can use his backyard? He has a huge yard and a grill.
Man: That could work! But you'd have to plan the food and decorations yourself. When is her actual birthday?
Woman: It's Friday, but everyone's busy on weekdays, so Saturday is better. I'm planning to tell her I'm taking her out for a nice dinner, then bring her to Tyler's house instead.
Man: Perfect. What kind of food does she like?
Woman: She loves Mexican food - tacos, guacamole, all that. Maybe I could get one of those taco trucks to cater? That would be fun and not too expensive.
Man: Great idea! Taco trucks are really popular. What about a cake? She loves chocolate cake, right?
Woman: Yes, the richer the better. I'll order one from that bakery she loves on 5th Street.
Man: What about decorations? Balloons, a birthday banner, maybe some photos of you two?
Woman: I can pick up balloons and a banner from the party store. I was also thinking of making a photo slideshow of pictures from our trips together.
Man: That's really cute! She'll love that. Do you want to have a theme?
Woman: She loves traveling, so maybe a travel theme with globes and maps? That could be cool.
Man: Perfect. I can help you decorate on Saturday if you want. And I'll make sure everyone gets there before you arrive with Emma so she doesn't see anyone before the surprise.
Woman: That would be amazing. Thank you so much, Josh. I owe you one.
Man: Don't worry about it. I'm just happy to help. It's going to be great.
Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
8. Why does the man want to have the party at Tyler's house instead of a restaurant?
9. What kind of food does Emma love?
10. What theme is the man considering for the party?
11. What does the woman offer to help with?

transcript.heading: Conversation Two (British Male + British Female)
paras: Man (Liam): Hi Olivia, I heard you're looking for a new laptop. What happened to your old one?
Woman (Olivia): Hi Liam, it died yesterday. It was seven years old, so I guess it was time. But there are so many options - I don't know what to get.
Man: What do you mainly use your laptop for? That will help narrow it down.
Woman: Mostly writing papers, browsing the internet, watching movies, and streaming music. I don't play video games or do any video editing or anything like that.
Man: Then you probably don't need the most powerful or expensive model. What's your budget?
Woman: I'm a student, so I don't want to spend more than around six hundred pounds if possible.
Man: That's reasonable. Are you set on a particular operating system - Windows or Mac?
Woman: I've always used Windows, but I've heard Macs are really good too. But Macs are so expensive - I don't think I can afford a new one on my budget.
Man: You could get a refurbished Mac for a bit less, but Windows laptops give you more options in your price range. Do you need it to be lightweight so you can carry it to class?
Woman: Yes, that's important. I carry it around campus every day, so I don't want something too heavy. And good battery life is a must - I don't always have time to charge it between classes.
Man: Then you should look for something with at least eight hours of battery life. There are some really good ultrabooks that are light and have great battery life. What screen size do you prefer?
Woman: My old one was fifteen inches, which was a bit big to carry. Maybe thirteen or fourteen inches would be better.

Man: Let me think - there are a few brands that make good budget laptops. The new Acer models are supposed to be really good for the price, and Lenovo makes reliable laptops too. Have you looked at any online reviews?
Woman: I started to, but there are so many it's overwhelming. All the brands say their laptop is the best.

Man: Maybe we could go to the electronics store after class tomorrow, and you can try out a few models in person to see how they feel. The keyboard and touchpad are really important - you want them to feel comfortable when you're typing.
Woman: That would be great. I'd really appreciate a second opinion. Should we go around three?
Man: Perfect, I'm free after my two o'clock class. And don't forget to ask about student discounts - most places offer ten or fifteen percent off if you show your student ID.
Woman: I definitely will. Thanks, Liam! You're a lifesaver.

transcript.heading: Passage One (British Male)
paras: The umbrella is such a common everyday object that few people stop to think about its long and surprisingly fascinating history. While we think of umbrellas primarily as protection from rain, they were originally used to shade people from the sun. The earliest known umbrellas date back over four thousand years to ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, and China, where they were made from palm leaves, feathers, or paper attached to wooden frames. In these early civilizations, umbrellas were a symbol of status and power - only royalty and nobles were allowed to use them, and special attendants would hold them over rulers to shade them from the sun.

Umbrellas as rain protection became more common in Europe by the 17th and 18th centuries, though they were initially considered only appropriate for women. The first man to regularly carry an umbrella in London, Jonas Hanway, faced ridicule and insults from coach drivers who saw him as a threat to their business, but he persisted for thirty years, and by the time of his death in 1786, umbrellas had become acceptable for men as well. Early umbrellas were heavy and awkward, with frames made of whalebone or wood that didn't fold easily. The modern folding umbrella with a steel frame wasn't invented until the 1850s, making umbrellas truly portable.

Today, billions of umbrellas are manufactured every year, ranging from inexpensive disposable models to high-end designer versions. Despite their simplicity, umbrellas continue to evolve - recent innovations include hands-free umbrellas that attach to your shoulder, wind-resistant models that don't turn inside out, and even umbrellas with built-in lights and phone chargers. Yet the basic purpose remains the same as it was four thousand years ago: protecting people from the elements.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (American Female)
paras: Color plays a powerful role in how we feel, think, and behave, often influencing us without our conscious awareness. This field, known as color psychology, is used by marketers, interior designers, hospitals, schools, and even sports teams to create specific moods and influence decisions. While reactions to color can be personal based on experience and culture, some associations are fairly universal.

Warm colors like red, orange, and yellow tend to evoke strong emotions. Red, for example, is associated with energy, passion, and urgency - it can raise heart rate and blood pressure slightly, which is why it's often used for clearance sales and stop signs. Restaurants frequently use red in their decor and branding because it's thought to stimulate appetite. Orange and yellow are cheerful, attention-grabbing colors associated with happiness and warmth, though bright yellow can be overwhelming in large quantities.

Cool colors like blue, green, and purple tend to have a calming effect. Blue is the most popular color worldwide and is associated with trust, reliability, and tranquility - which is why many banks, hospitals, and social media sites use blue in their logos. Green, the color of nature, is associated with health, growth, and freshness, making it a popular choice for environmentally friendly brands. Purple has long been associated with royalty and luxury, though lighter shades like lavender feel more peaceful and creative.

Neutral colors like black, white, gray, and brown can create subtle effects too - black signals sophistication and power, white feels clean and open, gray provides balance, and brown feels earthy and stable. It's important to note that cultural context matters: while white symbolizes purity and weddings in Western cultures, it's associated with funerals and mourning in some Eastern cultures. Understanding these associations can help you choose colors for your home, clothing, or presentations to create the effect you want.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Male)
paras: When most people think about volunteering, they think about helping others and contributing to their community. While these are certainly important benefits, volunteering also provides substantial professional advantages that can boost your career, whether you're a student just starting out or an established professional looking to advance.

One of the most valuable career benefits of volunteering is the opportunity to develop new skills and gain experience in areas you might not encounter at work or school. If you're interested in moving into project management, organizing a fundraiser for a local charity gives you hands-on experience planning budgets, coordinating teams, and managing timelines. If you want to improve your public speaking, volunteer to present at community events or lead volunteer training sessions. These practical experiences can be just as valuable as formal training, and they give you concrete examples to discuss in job interviews.

Volunteering is also one of the best ways to expand your professional network. You'll meet people from diverse backgrounds and industries who you might never encounter through your usual work or social circles. Many people find job opportunities through connections made while volunteering - nonprofit board members, fellow volunteers, and community leaders are often happy to recommend people they've worked with in a volunteer capacity, having seen their work ethic and skills firsthand.

Additionally, volunteering demonstrates initiative and character to employers. Listing volunteer experience on your resume shows that you're well-rounded, community-minded, and willing to take on challenges outside of required work. In competitive job markets, volunteer experience can set you apart from other candidates with similar qualifications. Finally, volunteering can help you explore new career paths without committing to a job change - volunteering at an animal shelter might help you realize you want to work with animals, or helping build houses might spark an interest in construction or community development.
